To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bacteriocin of Lactobacillales depletes the proton motive force in the sensitive organisms in an energy-independent fashion, whereas nisin depletes the same force in a concentration-dependent and energy-dependent manner.
four bacteriocins of the pediocin family, leuconcin S, and lactacion F, deplete the proton motive force of sensitive organisms, and the activity of these bacteriocins is energy independent.
bacteriocins from LAB act by dissipation of the proton motive force, a process that is independent of the energy requirements of the target cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of bacteriocins of the lactic acid bacteria, which are of interest as food preservatives and as therapeutic agents.
the development of bacteriocins as antimicrobial agents.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of bacteriocins from Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis, Lactobacilli, and Pediococci.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacteriocins of LAB act in an energy-dependent or -independent fashion, depending on the target organism.
bacteriocins of LAB act on the PMF of sensitive organisms in an energy-independent way, which results in the dissipation of the PMF.
the bacteriocin-induced dissipation of PMF is the common mechanism for the bacteriocins from LAB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bacteriocin-induced membrane permeabilization is the primary event in the killing process, and this is followed by the release of the intracellular components.
the bacteriocin activity is a function of the proton motive force and that the bacteriocinin molecule does not need to be energized for its activity.
the bacteriocin activity of lactic acid bacteriocins is independent of the proton motive force.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of the action of these bacteriocins is not energy dependent.
the PMF is a target for all bacteriocins from LAB, regardless of whether the bacteriocin is a class I (pediocin-like, nisin, and leuconcin S) or a class II (lactacin F-like bacteriocins) peptide.
bacteriocins from LAB share a common mechanism.
